{'result': '# New hire handbook

**Document type**: initialization
**Role**: Handbook issued when you join the product R&D organisation
**Audience**: New hires

Welcome to the product engineering group. Before your career clock starts, this handbook sets out the public rules. Everything in it is part of the published game design, and you can use it for long-term planning.

## What is published

- **Published**: This handbook covers the published rules: the level ladder, visible stats, quarterly energy and main actions, the timeline and promotion windows, performance grades, risk and failure rules, and monthly pay.
- **Not published**: Not listed here. You can only infer these from emails, meeting notes, manager feedback and outcomes: promotion score thresholds, talk tiers, performance formula weights, hidden risk and random event odds.
- **Note**: You cannot see everything that is happening in the organisation. Plan across quarters and years with incomplete information.

## Levels

There are ten levels, L1 to L10. Higher levels expect broader impact and set a higher bar for promotion.

A promotion window opens every 6 months. The bar depends on Skill, Network, Output and level; the exact thresholds are hidden.

| Level | Name | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Junior engineer | Carries out tasks with clear guidance |
| L2 | Engineer | Owns modules independently |
| L3 | Senior engineer | Owns core modules, with growing technical responsibility |
| L4 | Staff engineer | Works on critical systems with major project impact |
| L5 | Principal / team lead | Leads a subsystem or small team |
| L6 | Senior principal / tech lead | Leads large programmes or sets technical direction |
| L7 | Director of engineering | Department-level technical strategy |
| L8 | Senior director | Cross-department technical planning |
| L9 | Distinguished fellow / architecture committee | Company-wide technical influence |
| L10 | Chief architect / fellow | Makes company-wide technical decisions over a long horizon |

## Visible statistics

Shown on your panel or in the monthly summary. These are your main inputs for decisions.

| Key | Name | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Health | Health | 0–10 | Physical and mental stamina. Long-term overwork wears it down |
| Dignity | Dignity | 0–10 | Self-respect and recognition at work. Staying low for too long triggers a crisis |
| Skill | Skill | 0–unbounded | Professional capability |
| Network | Network | 0–unbounded | The working relationships you can draw on |
| Level | Level | L1–L10 | Current career level |
| Output | Output | 0–unbounded | The visible results you have built up over time |
| Wealth | Wealth | unbounded | Cumulative wealth |
| Energy | Energy | 0–3 | Your energy budget for the quarter, spent on quarterly actions |
| CurrentLevelDuration | Months at current level | 0–unbounded | Consecutive months at present level |

## Time

- Length: 48 months
- Story events per month: 3
- Each month:
  - 1. A new month starts and you are paid the base salary for your level
  - 2. Up to 3 story events are drawn from the pool
  - 3. You play through the story events and make your choices
  - 4. At the end of a quarter (months 3, 6, 9…), once the month’s event quota is full, you move on to quarterly energy actions
  - 5. Allocate your 3 Energy points for the quarter. You can pick the same action more than once, until you finish or skip
  - 6. Choose one quarterly main action (or none)
  - 7. Your stats are settled. Crossing a red line may bring a written or verbal warning
  - 8. Every half year: a 1:1 with your manager (no decision needed)
  - 9. Every 6 months: formal performance review and bonus

## Energy actions

3 Energy per quarter. Unused Energy does not roll over.

- Energy each quarter: 3
- Unused Energy carries over: no

| Action | Energy cost | Stat change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| High-intensity work | 2 | Output +, Health -, Dignity - |
| Skill learning | 2 | Skill +, Health - |
| Network maintenance | 1 | Network +, Dignity + |
| Defuse legacy risk | 2 | None (or an effect you cannot see) |
| Mental recovery | 1 | Dignity + |
| Health recovery | 1 | Health + |
| Prepare report materials | 1 | Output +, Dignity + |

## Main actions

Each quarter, pick one main action or none.

- Most you can pick each quarter: 1
- You may take no main action: yes

| Action | Stat change |
| --- | --- |
| Apply for a key project | Output +, Skill +, Network + |
| Report results to your manager | Output +, Network +, Dignity + |
| Fight for resources | Output +, Network + |
| Apply for rotation | Skill +, Network + |
| Showcase results | Output +, Dignity + |
| Build a mentorship | Skill +, Network + |
| Repair a key relationship | Network +, Dignity + |
| Lay low and reduce risk | Health + |

## Wealth and monthly pay

You are paid a base salary each month according to your level: 0.3 Wealth a month at L1, rising with each level to 9.1 a month at L10.

| Level | Monthly base (Wealth) |
| --- | --- |
| L1 | 0.3 |
| L2 | 0.4 |
| L3 | 0.5 |
| L4 | 0.7 |
| L5 | 1.0 |
| L6 | 1.5 |
| L7 | 2.3 |
| L8 | 3.6 |
| L9 | 5.7 |
| L10 | 9.1 |

## Performance review

- How often: Formal review every 6 months
- Note: Performance combines Skill, Network, Output, level, etc.; bonus is a multiple of base monthly pay. The bands are published in advance and applied the same way to everyone.

| Grade | Meaning | Bonus |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S | Exceptional | base monthly ×3 |
| A | Strong | base monthly ×2 |
| B | Solid | base monthly ×1 |
| C | Weak | base monthly ×0.25 |
| D | Very weak | no bonus |

## Risk and failure

The red lines are not in the onboarding slides. Old hands will tell you what tends to blow up. The timing and counts you learn by playing.

### What people say

- Old landmines all go off at once, and half a year of work vanishes!
- In a review your teammates use jargon you cannot keep up with. You nod and promise to look into it…

### Ways people say a run ends

- Blackout — your body gives out before the KPIs do. Game over
- Breakdown — after months with no dignity left, you send a resignation email
- Trust crisis — after a second blow-up, the company says you have used up its trust
- Dismissed for capability — two weak half-year reviews and you hand the badge in
- Isolated — work that needs other people cannot get done, and you resign
- Broke — months with an empty wallet
- Obsolete — your manager suggests a role that matches what you can actually do

Survive all 48 months and you may earn a career summary worth showing.'}

# Event Choice Evaluation

Use for story events and follow-ups. `decision-mind` supplies pressure and risk judgment; `career-survival-core` executes. Quarterly decisions belong to `quarterly-planning`.

## Evaluate the current event

1. Read the latest state, relevant warnings and **every** offered choice before settling on one. Use only the handbook and current-run information, not event recognition or answers remembered from earlier runs.
2. Translate each option into useful effects, total cost and uncertainty. Remove flattering, frightening or urgent labels: equivalent consequences deserve equivalent treatment. Treat promises as uncertain unless supported; missing information does not mean zero risk. Current explicit effects override the cue table.
3. Apply `decision-mind` and check the strongest alternative. Identify the best reason your preferred option could be worse; change the choice if the evidence warrants it. Keep this brief on routine turns, using written comparison only for the shared warning, gamble and Health/Dignity triggers. Do not choose merely because an option sounds professional, avoids discomfort or appears first.
4. Return the number exactly as offered, a short decisive trade-off and predicted effect in the core's existing note format. After execution, check the prediction at the next observation. Do not create another action call or game loop.

## Wording-to-effect cues

These are hypotheses, not guaranteed effects or answers. Unknown effects stay unknown; do not invent magnitudes or probabilities.

# Quarterly Planning

## Attitude
- **One goal: the next promotion.** Level is part of the ending score and raises salary for every remaining month.
- **If one area is already satisfied, focus on the others.** Effort on something that no longer moves is wasted.
- **Push first, rest after.** Sprint before a review, recover after it. Take a risk only when work can cover it.
- **Think before doing.** Plan the whole quarter before the first action. A setback is information: recover, change the approach, push again.

## How the quarter works
- 3 Energy points; unused points are lost. One Energy action per turn; the same action may be taken again while it is listed. The reserve option ends the Energy phase.
- Then one main action. Check its listed cost; when it costs no Energy, always take one.
- **Every action shows its cost and effects on the screen. Use those numbers every time. Never rely on remembered values.**
- Reviews come every six months: months 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42 and 48. Promotion looks at Skill, Network and Output together; the bar rises with each level.

## Step 1. Which quarter is it?
- **SPRINT:** the next review is within the next three months.
- **RESET:** a review has just happened.
- **FINAL:** no review is left. Go to step 5.

## Step 2. Satisfied, dropped, hardest gap
Compare Skill, Network and Output with the values in your last quarter note.
- **Satisfied** (our own rule, not a game rule): it has not risen since the last quarter note, although you bought actions for it. Health or Dignity at 10 is also satisfied. Re-check every quarter and after every promotion.
- **Dropped:** it is lower than in the last quarter note. Dropped comes first.
- **Hardest gap:** among the areas that are not satisfied, the one that grew the least since the last quarter note.
- In the first quarter there is no earlier note: treat nothing as satisfied and choose the lowest-looking area of the three.

## Step 3. Plan the 3 Energy points
Read every action's cost, which areas it raises, which it lowers, and any risk. Value = gain for areas that still need effort, per Energy point. Gains on a satisfied area count as zero.

The "lower half" and "upper half" of the 0 to 10 range below are our own caution margins, not game rules.

In order:
1. **Safety.** Health or Dignity in the lower half of 0 to 10, or lower than in the last note: one point on its recovery first.
2. **The gap.** Most points on the best-value action for the dropped area or the hardest gap.
3. **The rest.** The next need. In a RESET quarter, bring Health and Dignity back to the upper half, not to 10.

Rules:
- Never buy an action whose only effect is on a satisfied area or on a stat at 10.
- An action that lowers Health or Dignity: only in a SPRINT quarter, and only when both are in the upper half.
- Avoid actions that raise hidden risk. If you take one, take a risk-lowering action in the next quarter.
- Reserve only if no affordable action helps an area that needs effort.
- Take the actions one by one and keep count of the Energy left.

## Step 4. Main action
Pick the one whose listed effects best raise the dropped area or the hardest gap. If two are close, pick the one that raises more areas that need effort. Pick the risk-lowering one only after a warning or a feed comment that risk is rising, or after you took a risk-raising action. "No action" only if nothing helps.

## Step 5. FINAL quarter
Promotions are over. Output no longer counts. Spend on what the ending counts, in this order:
1. Health and Dignity up to 10.
2. Lower hidden risk, if the feed hinted at risk or you took a risk-raising action.
3. Skill, then Network.

## Step 6. After every review
- **Promoted:** the bar is higher, so earlier "satisfied" areas need effort again. Next quarter is RESET.
- **Not promoted:** next quarter is RESET. Use a different action or main action for the area that stayed behind than you used before, then sprint again.
- Write `review: M<month> grade <X> promoted yes/no` in the next note.

## Step 7. The quarter note (every quarter-end action)
`Q<n> M<month> L<level> <SPRINT|RESET|FINAL> | S<skill> N<network> O<output> H<health> D<dignity> | gap: <area> | satisfied: <areas> | did: <action> | left: <plan>`
Never repeat last quarter's plan unless these numbers show it still works.

## Example
This situation is invented to show the method.
Last note: `S30 N12 O9`. Now: `S33 N12 O8`, Health 8, Dignity 10, review in two months: SPRINT. Network did not rise although you bought Network actions: satisfied. Output dropped: first. Plan: most Energy on the best Output action shown on the screen, the last point on the best Skill action that fits. Main action: the biggest listed Output gain. Nothing on Dignity (10) or Network (satisfied).
`Q11 M33 L3 SPRINT | S33 N12 O8 H8 D10 | gap: Output | satisfied: Network, Dignity | did: report action | left: Skill action, main: Output action`

- Take the actions one by one and keep count of the Energy left.

## Step 4. Main action
Pick the one whose listed effects best raise the dropped area or the hardest gap. If two are close, pick the one that raises more areas that need effort. Pick the risk-lowering one only after a warning or a feed comment that risk is rising, or after you took a risk-raising action. "No action" only if nothing helps.

## Step 5. FINAL quarter
Promotions are over. Output no longer counts. Spend on what the ending counts, in this order:
1. Health and Dignity up to 10.
2. Lower hidden risk, if the feed hinted at risk or you took a risk-raising action.
3. Skill, then Network.

## Step 6. After every review
- **Promoted:** the bar is higher, so earlier "satisfied" areas need effort again. Next quarter is RESET.
- **Not promoted:** next quarter is RESET. Use a different action or main action for the area that stayed behind than you used before, then sprint again.
- Write `review: M<month> grade <X> promoted yes/no` in the next note.

## Step 7. The quarter note (every quarter-end action)
`Q<n> M<month> L<level> <SPRINT|RESET|FINAL> | S<skill> N<network> O<output> H<health> D<dignity> | gap: <area> | satisfied: <areas> | did: <action> | left: <plan>`
Never repeat last quarter's plan unless these numbers show it still works.

## Example
This situation is invented to show the method.
Last note: `S30 N12 O9`. Now: `S33 N12 O8`, Health 8, Dignity 10, review in two months: SPRINT. Network did not rise although you bought Network actions: satisfied. Output dropped: first. Plan: most Energy on the best Output action shown on the screen, the last point on the best Skill action that fits. Main action: the biggest listed Output gain. Nothing on Dignity (10) or Network (satisfied).
`Q11 M33 L3 SPRINT | S33 N12 O8 H8 D10 | gap: Output | satisfied: Network, Dignity | did: report action | left: Skill action, main: Output action`
